title: Hepatocellular Carcinoma
subtitle: StewardMD ONCOTREE Navigator (NCCN Guidelines Version 2.2026)
provenanceNote: Comprehensive NCCN v2.2026 (NCCN Guidelines Version 2.2026) clinical navigator for Hepatocellular Carcinoma. Full pathway: diagnostic workup (ACR LI-RADS imaging, AFP, Child-Pugh / ALBI, variceal screening, viral serologies) -> diagnostic confirmation -> Child-Pugh + performance status -> BCLC stage -> stage-directed arms, each refined by response / line of therapy before a recommendation. Curative arms: resection for solitary tumor without vascular invasion with preserved function, liver transplantation within Milan criteria (solitary <= 5 cm, or up to 3 lesions each <= 3 cm, no macrovascular invasion or extrahepatic spread), thermal ablation (RFA / MWA) for tumors <= 3 cm (Category 1), and downstaging toward transplant. Intermediate BCLC B: TACE or Y-90 radioembolization, then response / refractoriness triage. Advanced disease: preferred Category 1 first-line atezolizumab + bevacizumab (IMbrave150; variceal screening required) or durvalumab + tremelimumab STRIDE single high-dose priming (HIMALAYA; preferred when bevacizumab / bleeding risk contraindicated), with lenvatinib (REFLECT) or sorafenib (SHARP) as Category 1 alternatives when immunotherapy is contraindicated; biomarker-directed subsequent lines cabozantinib (CELESTIAL), regorafenib post-sorafenib (RESORCE), ramucirumab for AFP >= 400 ng/mL (REACH-2), or nivolumab + ipilimumab. Regimen options reference existing StewardMD Standard Protocols where available; agents without a matching protocol are shown as checklist guidance with NO dose. Workup / staging / surveillance wording is standard oncology, not proprietary guideline text. DRAFT - not clinically activated; the physician decides and the existing dose engine computes patient doses.
sourceNote: Structured in accordance with NCCN Clinical Practice Guidelines in Oncology (NCCN Guidelines) for Hepatocellular Carcinoma Version 2.2026 (August 14, 2026).

a.text: Preferred Category 1 first-line options for advanced Child-Pugh A disease with adequate performance status: atezolizumab + bevacizumab (IMbrave150) or durvalumab + tremelimumab STRIDE single high-dose priming (HIMALAYA; preferred when bevacizumab / bleeding risk is contraindicated). Screen for and manage esophageal varices before starting any bevacizumab-containing regimen because of the anti-VEGF bleeding risk.

b.text: Systemic therapy data are strongest in Child-Pugh A. Child-Pugh B is under-represented in trials; treat selectively with close monitoring and avoid systemic anticancer therapy in decompensated (Child-Pugh C) liver disease.

c.text: Using ACR LI-RADS criteria on multiphase contrast CT or dynamic contrast liver MRI: LR-5 is definitive for HCC without biopsy in patients with cirrhosis or chronic HBV. Biopsy is reserved for indeterminate lesions or a non-cirrhotic, non-HBV liver.

d.text: Transplant candidacy is generally judged against accepted size / number thresholds (e.g. Milan criteria); tumors beyond criteria may be considered for downstaging before listing, with a defined observation interval to select favorable biology.

nodes.name: Initial workup
nodes.title: Initial workup and baseline assessment
nodes.description: Baseline evaluation before staging: confirm the lesion, characterize liver function, and assess extent.

bullets.label: Multiphase contrast CT or dynamic contrast liver MRI using ACR LI-RADS criteria
bullets.sub: LR-5 is definitive for HCC without biopsy in cirrhosis or chronic HBV; chest CT for extent; assess portal vein for tumor thrombus

bullets.label: Serum Alpha-Fetoprotein (AFP) baseline quantification
bullets.sub: repeat for trend at each restaging; AFP >= 400 ng/mL selects ramucirumab in later lines

bullets.label: Liver function assessment: Child-Pugh class (A, B, C) and ALBI score (albumin-bilirubin)
bullets.sub: portal hypertension signs: splenomegaly, ascites, thrombocytopenia <100k; ICG clearance or HVPG where resection is planned

bullets.label: Screening upper endoscopy (EGD) within 6 months with banding of high-risk varices
bullets.sub: required before starting VEGF inhibitors (bevacizumab) because of bleeding risk

bullets.label: Viral hepatitis serologies with HBV DNA and HCV RNA
bullets.sub: start or continue antiviral suppression therapy; hepatology co-management

options.label: Diagnostic Workup Reviewed — Proceed to BCLC Staging & Functional Assessment

nodes.name: Presentation
nodes.title: Clinical presentation / care phase
nodes.description: Select the current clinical situation to enter the correct pathway.

nodes.name: Diagnostic confirmation
nodes.title: Confirming the diagnosis
nodes.description: In an at-risk cirrhotic liver, imaging alone can confirm HCC; otherwise biopsy is needed.
bullets: ACR LI-RADS 5 (arterial hyperenhancement with washout) on multiphase CT or dynamic MRI is definitive for HCC without biopsy in cirrhosis or chronic HBV
Biopsy for indeterminate lesions or a non-cirrhotic, non-HBV liver
Re-enter staging once the diagnosis is established

nodes.name: Tissue / repeat imaging
nodes.title: Indeterminate lesion: biopsy or short-interval re-imaging
nodes.description: Resolve the diagnosis before committing to cancer-directed therapy.
bullets: Image-guided core biopsy of the indeterminate lesion
Alternatively short-interval repeat multiphasic imaging to reassess LI-RADS category
Re-enter staging once the diagnosis is established

nodes.name: Liver function / PS
nodes.title: Child-Pugh class and performance status
nodes.description: Underlying liver reserve and performance status constrain every treatment decision in HCC.
bullets: Grade liver reserve by Child-Pugh class (A, B, C) and ALBI score (albumin-bilirubin)
Record portal hypertension signs: splenomegaly, ascites, thrombocytopenia <100k, known varices
Where resection is planned, confirm normal bilirubin with ICG clearance or HVPG <= 10 mmHg

options.label: Child-Pugh C or poor PS / decompensated

nodes.name: Supportive care / transplant eval
nodes.title: Decompensated or terminal: supportive care (transplant if eligible)
nodes.description: Child-Pugh C or terminal-stage disease: prioritize liver transplant evaluation where feasible, otherwise best supportive care.
bullets: Liver transplant evaluation if tumor burden and candidacy allow (best option for decompensated cirrhosis with limited tumor)
Otherwise best supportive / palliative care and symptom control
Manage ascites, encephalopathy and nutrition; hepatology co-management
Systemic anticancer therapy is generally not appropriate in Child-Pugh C

nodes.name: BCLC stage
nodes.title: BCLC stage
nodes.description: Assign the Barcelona Clinic Liver Cancer stage from tumor burden, vascular invasion / spread, and performance status.

tables.title: BCLC stage summary (simplified)
rows: Single, or up to 3 nodules <= 3 cm, no vascular invasion
Portal vein tumor thrombus and/or extrahepatic spread

nodes.name: Early-stage choice
nodes.title: BCLC 0 / A: curative-intent option
nodes.description: Choose among curative options by resectability, liver reserve, portal hypertension, and transplant candidacy.

bullets.label: Resection
bullets.sub: solitary tumor without vascular invasion, Child-Pugh A with normal bilirubin, ICG clearance or HVPG <= 10 mmHg

bullets.label: Thermal ablation (RFA or MWA)
bullets.sub: tumors <= 3 cm, Category 1; non-surgical candidate or alternative to resection

bullets.label: Transplant
bullets.sub: within Milan criteria, especially with impaired liver function

bullets.label: Downstaging / bridging
bullets.sub: beyond criteria but a potential transplant candidate

nodes.name: Resection
nodes.title: Surgical resection
nodes.description: Preferred curative option for a solitary tumor without vascular invasion and well-preserved liver function (Child-Pugh A, normal bilirubin, ICG clearance or HVPG <= 10 mmHg). Next: assess pathology-based recurrence risk.
bullets: Solitary tumor without macrovascular invasion; anatomic partial hepatectomy with an adequate future liver remnant
Confirm Child-Pugh A with normal bilirubin and ICG clearance, or HVPG <= 10 mmHg (no clinically significant portal hypertension)
Continue antiviral therapy for viral hepatitis to protect the remnant
Then assess resection pathology for recurrence risk (next step)

nodes.name: Resection pathology risk
nodes.title: After resection: recurrence-risk features
nodes.description: Pathologic high-risk features (microvascular invasion, poor differentiation, large size / satellites, close margin) identify patients for adjuvant systemic therapy on protocol; others enter surveillance.
bullets: High-risk: microvascular invasion, poor differentiation, tumor > 5 cm or satellite nodules, narrow margin
Low-risk: single small tumor, no vascular invasion, wide margin
Adjuvant atezolizumab + bevacizumab may reduce recurrence in high-risk resected disease (IMbrave050-type data; still maturing)

nodes.name: Adjuvant systemic
nodes.title: Adjuvant systemic therapy after high-risk resection
nodes.description: High-risk resected disease: consider adjuvant immunotherapy-based systemic therapy, then surveillance.
bullets: Adjuvant atezolizumab + bevacizumab in Child-Pugh A high-risk resected disease (evidence still maturing; discuss uncertainty)
Screen for and manage varices before the anti-VEGF component; monitor for immune-related adverse events
Continue antiviral therapy and hepatology co-management
Dose protocol referenced below (adjuvant fixed-duration schedule); then enter surveillance

nodes.name: Transplant
nodes.title: Liver transplantation
nodes.description: Curative for early HCC within Milan criteria (solitary <= 5 cm, or up to 3 lesions each <= 3 cm, without macrovascular invasion or extrahepatic spread), treating both tumor and underlying cirrhosis. Then post-transplant surveillance.
bullets: List if within Milan criteria: solitary <= 5 cm, or up to 3 lesions each <= 3 cm, without macrovascular invasion or extrahepatic spread
Bridging therapy (ablation, TACE or radioembolization) to prevent dropout while waiting
Preferred over resection when liver function is impaired
Lifelong immunosuppression; then post-transplant surveillance (next step)

nodes.name: Ablation
nodes.title: Local ablation
nodes.description: Curative-intent thermal ablation (RFA or MWA) for tumors <= 3 cm (Category 1), especially when surgery is not suitable. Next: confirm complete ablation on response imaging.
bullets: Radiofrequency ablation (RFA) or microwave ablation (MWA) for tumors <= 3 cm (Category 1)
Comparable to resection for very small tumors in non-surgical candidates
Consider combining with TACE for tumors in the 3-5 cm range
Then assess ablation response (next step)

nodes.name: Ablation response
nodes.title: After ablation: response assessment
nodes.description: Post-ablation multiphasic imaging distinguishes complete ablation from residual viable tumor at the treated margin.
bullets: Complete ablation: no nodular arterial enhancement at the treated margin
Residual / local progression: enhancing tissue at or adjacent to the ablation zone
Re-ablation is often feasible for isolated residual disease

nodes.name: Repeat ablation
nodes.title: Residual after ablation: repeat local therapy
nodes.description: Isolated residual or locally progressive tumor after ablation: repeat ablation or locoregional therapy, then surveillance.
bullets: Repeat ablation for a residual nodule amenable to a further session
TACE for a residual lesion less suited to re-ablation
Re-confirm Child-Pugh A function before re-treatment
Then enter surveillance

nodes.name: Downstaging / bridging
nodes.title: Downstaging toward transplant / resection
nodes.description: Tumor beyond transplant criteria in an otherwise eligible patient: locoregional therapy to shrink burden into criteria. Next: reassess against criteria.
bullets: TACE or radioembolization (Y90) to reduce tumor burden
Enforce a defined observation interval to select favorable biology
Reassess resectability / transplant criteria after treatment
Then re-stage against criteria (next step)

nodes.name: Downstage response
nodes.title: After downstaging: re-stage against criteria
nodes.description: Re-imaging after downstaging determines whether tumor burden is now within transplant / resection criteria, or has failed to respond.
bullets: Within criteria and stable through the observation interval: proceed to listing / resection
No response or continued progression: treat as advanced disease
Re-check liver function and AFP trend before listing

nodes.name: List for transplant / resect
nodes.title: Successful downstaging: proceed to transplant / resection
nodes.description: Tumor downstaged into criteria and stable through observation: list for transplant (or resect if now feasible), then surveillance.
bullets: List for liver transplant once within criteria and biologically stable
Resection instead if the downstaged tumor is now resectable with adequate remnant
Continue bridging locoregional therapy to prevent waitlist dropout
Then enter surveillance

nodes.name: Intermediate choice
nodes.title: BCLC B: locoregional vs systemic
nodes.description: Unresectable intermediate (BCLC B), liver-confined multinodular disease without vascular invasion: transarterial locoregional therapy, or systemic if unsuitable.

bullets.label: TACE
bullets.sub: preserved function, liver-confined, amenable arterial supply

bullets.label: Systemic
bullets.sub: diffuse / bulky bilobar disease or TACE-unsuitable

nodes.name: TACE
nodes.title: Transarterial chemoembolization (TACE)
nodes.description: Standard first choice for unresectable intermediate (BCLC B), liver-confined multinodular HCC without vascular invasion. Next: assess response and refractoriness.
bullets: Transarterial chemoembolization with selective / superselective delivery to preserve non-tumor parenchyma
Repeat on-demand for viable disease; reassess response by imaging
Continue liver-function monitoring between sessions
Then assess response / refractoriness (next step)

nodes.name: Radioembolization
nodes.title: Transarterial radioembolization (Y90)
nodes.description: Selective internal radiation (transarterial radioembolization, TARE) for suitable unresectable intermediate (BCLC B) disease or as a bridging / downstaging tool. Next: assess response.
bullets: Pre-treatment mapping angiography and lung-shunt assessment
Lobar or segmental (radiation-segmentectomy) delivery
Option for bridging / downstaging toward transplant or resection
Then assess response / refractoriness (next step)

nodes.name: Locoregional response
nodes.title: After TACE / Y90: response vs refractoriness
nodes.description: Response imaging after locoregional therapy decides between continued locoregional treatment and a switch to systemic therapy for refractory / untreatable-progression disease.
bullets: Objective response / durable control: continue on-demand locoregional therapy
TACE-refractory / untreatable progression, or declining liver function: switch to systemic therapy
Avoid repeating locoregional therapy that would compromise liver reserve

nodes.name: Continue locoregional
nodes.title: Responding disease: continue locoregional therapy
nodes.description: Disease responding to TACE / Y90 with preserved liver function: continue on-demand locoregional therapy, then surveillance.
bullets: Repeat TACE / Y90 on-demand for viable disease
Reassess liver function before each session; stop if reserve declines
Consider adding systemic therapy for bilobar / progressive disease per multidisciplinary review
Then enter surveillance

nodes.name: First-line choice
nodes.title: Advanced disease: first-line systemic selection
nodes.description: For advanced / progressing disease with preserved liver function (Child-Pugh A), select the first-line backbone by immunotherapy eligibility and bleeding / autoimmune contraindications.

bullets.label: Atezolizumab + bevacizumab (IMbrave150) - preferred Category 1
bullets.sub: Child-Pugh A; screen and treat varices first (anti-VEGF bleeding risk)

bullets.label: Durvalumab + tremelimumab STRIDE (HIMALAYA) - preferred Category 1
bullets.sub: single high-dose tremelimumab priming; preferred when bevacizumab / bleeding risk is contraindicated

bullets.label: Lenvatinib (REFLECT) or sorafenib (SHARP) - Category 1 alternatives
bullets.sub: when immunotherapy is contraindicated; Child-Pugh A

options.label: IO-eligible, no bleeding risk (atezo + bev, IMbrave150)
IO-eligible but anti-VEGF contraindicated (durva + treme STRIDE)

nodes.name: Atezo + bev
nodes.title: First line: atezolizumab + bevacizumab (IMbrave150, preferred Category 1)
nodes.description: Preferred Category 1 first-line regimen (IMbrave150) for advanced HCC in Child-Pugh A patients without contraindications; requires variceal screening. Next: on-progression assessment.
bullets: Preferred Category 1 first-line backbone per IMbrave150; confirm Child-Pugh A and adequate performance status
Screening upper endoscopy (EGD) within 6 months with banding of high-risk varices before starting (bevacizumab bleeding risk)
Monitor for immune-related adverse events, proteinuria and hypertension
Dose protocol referenced below; then reassess on progression (next step)

nodes.name: Durva + treme
nodes.title: First line: durvalumab + tremelimumab STRIDE (HIMALAYA, preferred Category 1)
nodes.description: Preferred Category 1 first-line dual checkpoint option (HIMALAYA STRIDE single high-dose priming regimen); preferred when bevacizumab / bleeding risk is contraindicated. Next: on-progression assessment.
bullets: Preferred Category 1 per HIMALAYA: single high-dose (priming) dose of tremelimumab added to durvalumab, then durvalumab maintenance (STRIDE regimen)
Preferred when bevacizumab is contraindicated or bleeding risk is high; avoids anti-VEGF bleeding risk
Confirm Child-Pugh A and adequate performance status; monitor for immune-related adverse events
Dose protocol referenced below; then reassess on progression (next step)

nodes.name: First-line TKI
nodes.title: First-line TKI selection
nodes.description: When immunotherapy is contraindicated, choose the Category 1 oral multikinase inhibitor: lenvatinib (REFLECT) or sorafenib (SHARP).
bullets: Lenvatinib (REFLECT): weight-based dosing, often higher response rate
Sorafenib (SHARP): the reference first-line multikinase inhibitor
Confirm Child-Pugh A function before either

nodes.name: Lenvatinib
nodes.title: First line: lenvatinib (REFLECT, Category 1 alternative)
nodes.description: Oral multikinase inhibitor, non-inferior first-line TKI alternative to sorafenib (REFLECT, Category 1). Next: on-progression assessment.
bullets: Category 1 alternative per REFLECT; weight-based dosing; monitor blood pressure and thyroid function
Often preferred over sorafenib for a higher response rate
Confirm Child-Pugh A function; dose modify for toxicity
Dose protocol referenced below; then reassess on progression (next step)

nodes.name: Sorafenib
nodes.title: First line: sorafenib (SHARP, Category 1 alternative)
nodes.description: The reference first-line multikinase inhibitor for advanced HCC (SHARP, Category 1). Next: on-progression assessment.
bullets: Category 1 alternative per SHARP; monitor for hand-foot skin reaction, diarrhea, hypertension
Confirm Child-Pugh A function; dose modify for toxicity
Dose protocol referenced below
Then reassess on progression (next step)

nodes.name: On progression (1L)
nodes.title: After first-line: response, progression or intolerance
nodes.description: Restaging after first-line systemic therapy directs continued treatment, a switch to second-line, or a tolerability-driven switch.
bullets: Ongoing response / stable disease: continue first-line therapy
Radiographic progression: move to a second-line agent selected by the prior drug and AFP
Unacceptable toxicity with disease control: switch to a better-tolerated agent

nodes.name: Continue first line
nodes.title: Responding on first line: continue therapy
nodes.description: Continued benefit from first-line systemic therapy: maintain treatment with monitoring, then surveillance.
bullets: Continue the first-line regimen while benefit and tolerability persist
Restage every 8-12 weeks; monitor liver function and AFP trend
Manage immune-related or TKI toxicities with dose modification / supportive care
Then enter surveillance

nodes.name: Switch for intolerance
nodes.title: Intolerance with disease control: switch agent
nodes.description: Disease controlled but first-line therapy not tolerated: switch to a better-tolerated agent, then reassess as a subsequent line.
bullets: Switch to an alternative first-line agent with a different toxicity profile (e.g. IO to TKI or between TKIs)
Optimize supportive care and dose before abandoning an effective class
Re-confirm Child-Pugh A function
Then follow the second-line selection pathway (next step)

nodes.name: Second-line choice
nodes.title: Second-line systemic selection
nodes.description: After first-line progression in Child-Pugh A disease, select by the prior agent, AFP level, and immunotherapy eligibility.

nodes.name: Regorafenib
nodes.title: Second line: regorafenib post-sorafenib (RESORCE, Category 1)
nodes.description: Category 1 for patients who tolerated and then progressed on sorafenib (RESORCE). Next: on-progression assessment.
bullets: Category 1 per RESORCE, indicated specifically after sorafenib tolerance and progression
Monitor for hand-foot skin reaction, hypertension, hepatotoxicity
Confirm Child-Pugh A function
Dose protocol referenced below; then reassess on progression (next step)

nodes.name: Cabozantinib
nodes.title: Second / later line: cabozantinib (CELESTIAL, Category 1)
nodes.description: Multikinase inhibitor active after prior systemic therapy (CELESTIAL, Category 1). Next: on-progression assessment.
bullets: Category 1 per CELESTIAL; option after progression on one or two prior systemic agents
Monitor for hand-foot skin reaction, diarrhea, hypertension
Confirm Child-Pugh A function
Dose protocol referenced below; then reassess on progression (next step)

nodes.name: Ramucirumab
nodes.title: Second line: ramucirumab for AFP >= 400 (REACH-2, Category 1)
nodes.description: Biomarker-directed anti-VEGFR2 antibody (REACH-2, Category 1) for patients with baseline AFP at or above 400 ng/mL after first-line therapy. Next: on-progression assessment.
bullets: Biomarker-selected: baseline AFP >= 400 ng/mL (REACH-2, Category 1)
Monitor for hypertension and proteinuria
Confirm Child-Pugh A function
Dose protocol referenced below; then reassess on progression (next step)

nodes.name: Nivo + ipi
nodes.title: Second line: nivolumab + ipilimumab (dual checkpoint blockade)
nodes.description: Dual checkpoint inhibitor option after prior systemic therapy in IO-eligible Child-Pugh A disease. Next: on-progression assessment.
bullets: Nivolumab + ipilimumab dual checkpoint blockade after progression on prior systemic therapy (including prior TKI) in IO-eligible disease
Confirm Child-Pugh A function and adequate performance status; exclude active autoimmune disease and prior severe immune-related toxicity
Monitor closely for immune-related adverse events: colitis, hepatitis, pneumonitis, endocrinopathies
Checklist guidance only (no StewardMD dose protocol for this doublet in HCC); then reassess on progression (next step)

nodes.name: On progression (2L)
nodes.title: After second-line: further therapy or supportive care
nodes.description: Restaging after second-line therapy directs a further systemic line versus transition to best supportive care, gated by liver function and performance status.
bullets: Preserved Child-Pugh A and good PS: sequence a not-yet-used agent or trial
Declining liver function or poor PS: transition to best supportive care
Reassess AFP trend and symptom burden at each restaging

nodes.name: Third line
nodes.title: Third line and beyond
nodes.description: Sequential single-agent therapy after two prior lines in a fit patient, or a clinical trial.
bullets: Sequence a not-yet-used TKI (regorafenib / cabozantinib) or checkpoint inhibitor per prior exposure
Clinical trial where available
Reassess liver function and performance status before each new line
Transition to best supportive care when Child-Pugh declines or PS is poor

nodes.name: Best supportive care
nodes.title: Best supportive / palliative care
nodes.description: Declining liver function or performance status after systemic therapy: prioritize symptom control and quality of life.
bullets: Best supportive / palliative care with early palliative-care involvement
Manage ascites, encephalopathy, pain and nutrition; hepatology co-management
Further anticancer therapy is generally inappropriate once Child-Pugh C or poor PS
Advance-care planning and caregiver support

nodes.name: Recurrence
nodes.title: Recurrence after curative therapy
nodes.description: Recurrence after resection, ablation or transplant: re-stage and treat by pattern.
bullets: Re-image liver and chest; recheck AFP and liver function
Localized intrahepatic recurrence may be re-treated with curative or locoregional intent
Diffuse or extrahepatic recurrence is treated as advanced disease

nodes.name: Repeat local therapy
nodes.title: Localized recurrence: repeat local / locoregional therapy
nodes.description: Curative or locoregional re-treatment for isolated intrahepatic recurrence with preserved function, then surveillance.
bullets: Re-resection or ablation for isolated resectable / ablatable recurrence
Salvage transplant in selected candidates within criteria
TACE / radioembolization for multifocal but liver-confined recurrence
Then resume surveillance

nodes.name: Surveillance
nodes.title: Post-treatment surveillance / follow-up
nodes.description: Monitoring cadence after curative or locoregional therapy; escalate on recurrence.
bullets: Multiphasic CT / MRI and AFP every 3-6 months for the first 2 years, then every 6-12 months
Ongoing screening of the cirrhotic remnant liver for new primaries
Continue antiviral therapy and hepatology co-management
A confirmed new lesion or rising AFP enters the recurrence pathway
nodes.linkLabel: If recurrence is detected: go to the Recurrence pathway
